## Failure-driven maintenance

An optional `Gotchas` section in a skill source records observed failures. Use bullets of the form `- **<failure in ≤8 words>** — <rule>. Evidence: <record id or date>.` Never emit an empty section. Keep entries append-mostly; cross-task rules belong in their shared guide.

The loop is evidence-driven: run the agent on real work, dispatch `review-friction` for that agent over a time window to collect evidence records from its runs (friction review (see included section "Friction review contract")), then dispatch `review-skill` with the skill source, generated skill, intended contract, and the friction findings as its evidence records. The caller that started the loop reads the skill review, decides which corrections to make, and applies them in a writable Playbook checkout; nothing is filed elsewhere. An evidence record is a pointer plus a judgment: the path and line range of the run's session transcript (`<session>/<AgentId>.jsonl`, whose `session_init` entry carries the exact system prompt, task, tools, and model that ran) or an `omp --export` of it, the playbook commit the skill was built from (or, when that is unknown, the latest commit before the run), and the observed result. Do not paraphrase the skill revision; the transcript is the revision. Trace each finding to its editable owner: a task-specific procedural failure becomes a Gotchas entry, dispatch ambiguity tightens the agent description, and a mistaken activation boundary changes a routing case. Regenerate and inspect the affected skill, not its compiled copy. Check other consumers before changing shared guidance. Moved rules can change salience, and conditional reads may still be missed despite checked links; both are things to watch for in evidence records.

Bundled scripts are not used because read-only review agents cannot run `bash`.
